THIS WRIT PETITION IS FILED UNDER ARTICLES 226 AND 227 OF THE CONSTITUTION OF INDIA, PRAYING TO DECLARE THAT THE ACTION OF THE RESPONDENTS IN DEMOLISHING THE PORTION OF THE BUILDING EXISTED ON THE SCHEDULE PROPERTY TO THIS WRIT PETITION WITHOUT FOLLOWING THE PROCEDURES ESTABLISHED BY LAW AS ONE WITHOUT JURISDICTION AND WITHOUT AUTHORITY OF LAW AND ETC.,
 THIS WRIT PETITION COMING ON FOR PRELIMINARY HEARING IN 'B' GROUP, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:

2  ORDER

The petitioners in this writ petition are seeking for declaration that the action of the respondents in demolishing the portion of the building existed on the schedule property without following procedures established by law and is one without jurisdiction, also a direction to restore the portion of the building demolished by them to its original position prior to the demolition and direction to pay compensation of Rs.33,44,000/- to the petitioners for the damage caused in the schedule property.

2. Heard Sri. Rajendra .S, learned counsel for Sri. S.V. Prakash, learned counsel for the petitioners,
Sri. B.K. Manjunath, learned counsel for respondent No.8 and Smt. Anitha .N, learned HCGP for respondent Nos.1 to 7.
3.

The petitioners claim to be the absolute owners of the suit schedule property and portion of the schedule property bearing Katha No.215/182/212 facing old P.B. Road in Harihara city was demolished by the respondent- authorities without following the due process of law.

Learned counsel for the petitioners would contend that the action of the respondents in demolishing the portion of the building without following due process of law is in violation of Article 300-A and Article 21 of Constitution of India and that the petitioners are entitled for compensation.
4.

Learned counsel for the petitioners would contend that some owners before demolition obtained an interim order from this Court restraining the respondent-authorities from demolishing such buildings and certain other owners had challenged the illegal demolition and in one such W.P.
No.47843/2014, this Court has directed the respondent to initiate proceedings under the Act No.30 of 2013 and to determine not only the compensation but also rent, damages and other compensatory reliefs including the loss caused to the petitioners.
5.

Learned counsel for the petitioners would submit that placing reliance on the order in W.P.
No.47843/2014, another Co-Ordinate Bench of this Court in W.P. No.19433/2015 on similar facts,
which is squarely covered by the said order has disposed of the writ petition.
Learned counsel for the respondents does not dispute that the applicability of the order to the present facts and circumstances of the case.

6. The Co-Ordinate Bench of this Court in similar circumstances has held that if it is found that the property belonging to the petitioner has been utilized for the purpose of widening of the road, the petitioner is entitled for compensation in accordance with the provisions contained under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act,
2013 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act, 2013 for short).
7.

Accordingly, the writ petition stands disposed of directing respondent Nos.1 to 5 to conduct survey of the subject property after notifying the petitioners and after conducting the survey, if it is found that the portion of the property belonging to the petitioners has been utilized for the purpose of widening of old P.B. road, respondent Nos.1 to 5 are directed to initiate the proceedings for acquisition of the subject property under the Act, 2013 and determine not only compensation but also rent, damages and other such compensatory reliefs including the loss caused to the petitioners,
if they are entitled to in accordance with law.
The entire exercise to be concluded within six months from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.
